items.title: Roland announces AI-assisted melody-generation plug-in, Melody Flip
items.excerpt: Roland has launched Melody Flip, an AI-assisted melody-generation plug-in built with Sony CSL that is designed to work as a “music creation partner” rather than a one-click song generator. It reshapes the producer's own audio into new melodic, chord, bass and drum ideas inside the DAW.

items.title: AI ‘artists’ set to perform ‘live’ at first AI Music Awards in Los Angeles
items.excerpt: The first AI Music Awards will stage ‘live’ performances by AI-generated acts including Xania Monet in Los Angeles in November, with the human creators behind each ‘artist’ “directing the stage”. It is an early test of what live performance means when the performer is a model.

items.title: Suno admits to scraping YouTube audio data to train AI music models
items.excerpt: Lawyers for Suno conceded the platform trained on licensed music pulled by “circumvent[ing] YouTube’s encryption”, the clearest admission yet of where a mainstream music-generation model's training corpus came from.

items.title: Playhead builds custom effects chains from your sound descriptions
items.excerpt: Playhead is a new macOS tool that turns a plain-language description of a sound into an editable effect chain inside your DAW, complete with adjustable macro controls. It is prompt-to-signal-chain rather than prompt-to-song.

items.title: Two Legs, Five Arms is a FREE generative drum machine for macOS
items.excerpt: François Pé's free AU MIDI effect separates rhythmic density from character: you say how many notes to play, and the algorithm decides placement along a style axis running from house to rock, Afro-Cuban and hip-hop.

items.title: Sound designers and SFX libraries launch Professional Sound Alliance to fight AI scraping
items.excerpt: Sound designers and SFX library owners have formed the Professional Sound Alliance to push back on what it calls “Data Piracy” and “Sync Piracy” — unauthorised scraping of sound libraries for AI training and reuse. “Now sound will have protection of our own.”

items.title: AI artists will somehow play ‘live’ at their own awards ceremony in November
items.excerpt: AI-generated ‘artists’ including Xania Monet will ‘perform’ on stage at the inaugural AI Music Awards, raising the question of what staging, direction and liveness mean for a synthetic act.

items.title: Brian May on why he’s changed his mind on AI: “We have to resist”
items.excerpt: Queen's Brian May says he has reversed his earlier optimism about AI in music — “we have to control it very, very seriously and very quickly” — and explains why he has gone cold on the idea of a Queen avatar show.

items.title: ReSing Voices Vol 2 from IK Multimedia
items.excerpt: IK Multimedia expands its ReSing voice-transformation library with a second volume of AI vocal models, letting producers re-sing a recorded take in a different voice from inside the studio.

items.title: ElevenLabs strikes first deal with a major label to launch AI-powered music platform
items.excerpt: Universal Music Group and ElevenLabs have partnered on a licensed AI music platform and a line of AI audio products — the first major-label deal for the voice-AI company and a template for what ‘cleared’ generative tools may look like.

items.title: BandLab’s mastering capabilities just got an upgrade – here’s what’s new
items.excerpt: BandLab has upgraded its automated mastering engine with member-exclusive presets and far more control over mastering parameters, moving AI mastering from a black box toward an adjustable tool.

items.title: New Mac App, HarmonyKeen, Writes Harmony Parts To Your MIDI Melodies Using Music Theory, Not AI
items.excerpt: HarmonyKeen takes a monophonic MIDI melody and writes harmony parts around it, working out voice leading from music theory rather than a model — and markets that explicitly as a feature in an AI-saturated plugin market.

items.title: DistroKid’s $2 billion valuation based on it being a pipeline for AI slop, says Universal
items.excerpt: Universal claims DistroKid's $2bn valuation rests on it acting as a pipeline for AI-generated ‘slop’ and infringing uploads — a fight over what happens when generative output floods the same distribution rails human artists use.
